slides.author: Alexey Grigorev
slides.title: Running Durable Agents in Production
slides.subtitle: A DataTalksClub workshop with Nicholas Lotz on June 16.

slides.title: If you built a basic agent loop
slides.body: You probably saw the next questions quickly: where to store state, how to recover, how to wait for approval, and how to debug failures.

slides.title: Production needs the layer around the loop
slides.body: The agent loop plans, calls tools, and returns answers. The production layer handles state, retries, recovery, approvals, traces, and deployment.

slides.title: What we will cover
slides.body: Why in-process loops fail, how to persist workflow state, resume after process death, retry tool calls, and handle approval steps.

slides.title: What you will inspect
slides.body: LLM calls, tool calls, timing, token usage, errors, retry attempts, and the execution history needed to understand a failed run.

slides.title: Useful for real agent projects
slides.body: This applies to RAG, workflow automation, data tasks, customer operations, internal tools, evaluation, monitoring, and production AI systems.
